segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So some adjectives will exclusively go with estar. Some adjectives will exclusively go with ser.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Some adjectives can go with either ser or estar, and change their meaning, like aburrido, meaning bored as a state, or boring as a characteristic, just changing depending on whether it goes with ser or estar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Another example of a word like this is listo. Listo.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Listo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now listo, when it comes with estar, means ready. So how would you say I am ready?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy listo. Or lista, in my case.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Estoy lista or listo. How would you say we are ready?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estamos listos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And what if we were a female group?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estamos listas.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Estamos listas. And what if we wanted to emphasize we are ready?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Somos... no?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: You make it a characteristic and it's more emphatic! This is a very interesting idea.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Nosotros... That's what you said when I go too fast!

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: So it's nosotros estamos listas.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Mm, there's a contradiction there.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Nosotras estamos listas.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Yes. All-female group: nosotras estamos listas, or male or mixed group: nosotros estamos listos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, to be listo, to be ready, as a characteristic, means to be smart in Spanish.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, this is one of the words that we can use with ser or estar, and the meaning changes.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, estoy listo, I am ready. Soy listo, I'm smart. So, if you want to say he's smart, he is smart, how would you say it?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Es listo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Es listo. She is smart?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Es lista.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. You are smart, speaking informally to a woman.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: If you've forgot the you are, you can think of where are you from, that might help you trigger it: de dónde...

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Eres... eres lista.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. You are very smart.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Eres muy lista.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The word for so, like I'm so bored, or I'm so tired, is tan, T-A-N, tan.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Tan.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So how would you say I'm so tired?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy tan cansado... cansada.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Estoy tan cansado, estoy tan cansada. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say I am so bored?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy tan aburrida.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Estoy tan aburrido, aburrida.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say he is so bored?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Él está tan aburrido.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Está tan aburrido, or él está tan aburrido.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now, how would you say it is so boring? It is so boring. So boring, not bored. Boring.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Es tan aburrido.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Es tan aburrido.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The word for good in Spanish is bueno.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We've mentioned this before. We have in English "bon appétit", which is of course French, but we say it in English, and you can see the O of "bon appétit" splitting to become bueno in Spanish.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now, the meaning of bueno changes as well between ser and estar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: If you're talking about "it is", the change is a kind of change in feeling: es bueno, está bueno, a small change in feeling which really depends on dialect, so we won't look at it too much here, you will just listen.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But if you refer to people, in most dialects, if we use ser, we get the meaning of to be a good person, or to be good at something.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So if we want to say they are good, and you mean they are good people, or that they're good at something, how would you say it?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Son buenos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Son buenos. He is good?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Es bueno.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Es bueno. Now if you use estar, it will sound like he's attractive, he's in good form, huh? So bueno with estar, if we're talking about people, then gives you this meaning.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, how would you say that? He is good, meaning attractive, in good form?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Está bueno.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Está bueno.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So you see that you can have many different changes in shade of meaning between ser and estar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, other than the fact that we are being permitted and obliged to perceive and express the world in a certain way by Spanish, which is very interesting in itself, we also get the opportunity to use these different nuances between ser and estar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And when you really get your head around it, which is just through listening and observing and seeing how people are using it, you will probably feel that it's missing in English, that sometimes in English you might want to clarify not está, but es, and you can't do it.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So you realise that Spanish gives you a tool to relate to reality that in this case English doesn't give you. And this is one of the most fascinating and exciting things about language learning, not an obstacle to speaking the language.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We don't want to see it like this: "Oh, every time I use to be, I have to think about this characteristic or state business." No, we want to look at it from the other angle, about what it offers us.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say I want to know how he is, and we mean I want to know how is he doing?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiero saber cómo es.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How is he doing?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Oh. Cómo está.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Quiero saber cómo está. Now what would it mean, quiero saber cómo es? What would that mean?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: How he is, what he's like.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Exactly. I want to know what he's like. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Another adjective you can use with ser or estar is feliz. What do you think feliz might mean?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Happy.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And how do you know that?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ¡Feliz Navidad!

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Oh, okay. (laughs) Happy Christmas, ¡Feliz Navidad! But is there some connection in English that might might have helped you as well?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Did you hear "felicity" in English?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Ah, how would felicity be in Spanish?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Felicidad.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Felicidad, which means happiness. Happiness. So feliz, happy.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So feliz can also go with ser or estar to give the meaning of I'm happy, or I'm a happy person.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So we don't need to say I am a happy person, we can just use ser, ah? So like I said, there's no real way for you to know that other than listening. If you wanted to play safe, and say literally I'm a happy person, it would not be at all incorrect.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So firstly, how do you say I am happy as a state?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy feliz.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Estoy feliz. Now, I'm happy, and you mean as a characteristic?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Soy feliz.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Soy feliz. So this is fine, you can do this. But there's no real way for you to know whether feliz is an adjective that's flexible enough to be used with ser and estar. It really depends on the adjective itself, the word itself, rather than the meaning in many cases.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So with that insecurity, and wanting to give the meaning, you could have just said I am a happy person, and then you don't have to worry about it. So how would you say that?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Soy una persona feliz.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Soy una persona feliz. And that's also perfect Spanish. So there you could have said soy feliz or soy una persona feliz.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So to really get our heads around ser and estar, it's important to listen actively and to notice and see how people are using ser and estar, and making our own conclusions as to why, working with this base of state and characteristic. It's a process of listening. And the more you get intimate with this idea, it offers you a great range of expression that you don't have in English, and you should really enjoy it.
